title: Arguing a position
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: presente, L1-M6's - every main verb of the ten is in it
congiuntivo presente after a conjunction that governs it: sia, abbia, all L3-M3's forms and no new ones
gerundio, used adverbially and never with stare: essendo, avendo, sbagliando
passato prossimo where the ladder already owns the participle: ho capito, ho finito

rules.text: THESE CONJUNCTIONS TAKE THE CONGIUNTIVO WHATEVER THE SENTENCE MEANS. benché, sebbene and nonostante concede; a meno che concedes an exception; purché sets a condition; affinché states a purpose; prima che is the different-subject twin of L4-M6's prima di. The mood here is grammatical AGREEMENT, not doubt: the speaker can be completely certain and the verb still goes to the congiuntivo. That is the one thing to carry over from L4-M5, where the same forms meant something.

PUR PLUS THE GERUNDIO IS A WHOLE CONCESSION IN TWO WORDS. pur essendo d'accordo is although I agree; pur avendo ragione is although he is right. The gerund on its own is adverbial too - sbagliando ho capito, by getting it wrong I understood; essendo tardi, since it is late. You already own two of these forms: mangiando and parlando are L2-M7's, inside the stare plus gerundio progressive, and nothing about them changes here.

THE SCAFFOLD IS FIVE WORDS AND IT IS THE SHAPE OF THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. in primo luogo opens, in secondo luogo adds, d'altra parte turns, tuttavia answers the turn, in conclusione closes. innanzitutto is the everyday twin of in primo luogo. English signposts an argument with the same five moves in the same order, so nothing about the SHAPE has to be learned - only the words.

A MENO CHE CARRIES AN EXTRA NON THAT ENGLISH DOES NOT SAY. a meno che non ci sia un problema is unless there is a problem, NOT unless there is not a problem. The non is expletive - it belongs to the conjunction and it negates nothing. This is the second sighting of the trick L4-M6 taught on finché non, and the second sighting is what makes it believable.

TUTTAVIA OPENS ITS CLAUSE AND CANNOT SIT INSIDE IT. English however is mobile - the plan, however, failed - and tuttavia is not: it takes the front of the sentence, exactly as L4-M2's positional law said of the connectors it taught. Same law, new family. Put it first and stop looking for the comma-in-the-middle slot.

BENCHÉ AND ALTHOUGH ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF WORD, AND THERE IS NO MEANING UNDERNEATH TO REASON FROM. English although takes an ordinary verb; benché takes the congiuntivo because it is benché, full stop. A learner who hunts for a reason reads the concession as doubtful when the speaker is certain of it. Learn the list of triggers, not a theory.

sentences.display: In primo luogo, il fatto è che il problema non è il tempo
sentences.cue: First of all, the fact is that the problem is not time
sentences.literal: In first place, the fact is that the problem not is the time

words.cue: first of all, in the first place
words.note: The opening move of an argument, learned whole. innanzitutto is the everyday twin and says the same thing in one word.
Four words, one key. It sits on L3-M10's fatto but is learned whole, because it is a frame you drop a whole clause into.

sentences.trap: in primo luogo is not primo. The number word alone counts things; the three-word phrase orders an argument, and only the phrase does that job.
sentences.sound: in PRI-mo LUO-go, four syllables in luogo run as two: LWO-go. il FAT-to E ke.

variations.display: Innanzitutto, il problema non è il tempo
variations.cue: First of all, the problem is not time

variations.display: Il fatto è che il problema non è il tempo
variations.cue: The fact is that the problem is not time
variations.changed: the frame alone, with no ordering word

variations.display: In primo luogo, il problema è il tempo
variations.cue: First of all, the problem is time

mistake.display: Primo, il fatto è che il problema non è il tempo
mistake.why: Primo alone is the number. Opening a case takes in primo luogo or innanzitutto; primo on its own reads as a list of objects, not an argument.

sentences.usage: Opening a case in a meeting, or the first line of an argument you have thought about.
sentences.mnemonic: first PLACE, not first thing: luogo is the place in the argument.

sentences.display: In secondo luogo il lavoro è pesante. Ad esempio, nessuno dorme
sentences.cue: Secondly the work is heavy. For example, nobody sleeps
sentences.literal: In second place the work is heavy. To example, nobody sleeps

words.note: The second rung of the scaffold, built exactly like in primo luogo. Italian keeps counting this way and does not switch to a different shape.
The support move: it introduces the evidence for the point just made. ad rather than a before a vowel, and the pair is learned whole.

sentences.trap: ad esempio introduces evidence, never a new claim. If what follows is another point, it wants in secondo luogo instead.
sentences.sound: in se-CON-do LWO-go. ad e-SEM-pio, four syllables, stress on SEM.

variations.display: In secondo luogo il lavoro è pesante
variations.cue: Secondly the work is heavy
For example, nobody sleeps

mistake.display: In secondo, il lavoro è pesante
mistake.why: luogo is not optional. The scaffold word is the whole three-word phrase; in secondo by itself is not Italian.

sentences.usage: Adding the second point of a case, then backing it with one concrete fact.
sentences.mnemonic: same frame, new number: primo, secondo, luogo stays.

sentences.display: Benché tu abbia ragione, insisto: questa è la mia obiezione
sentences.cue: Although you are right, I insist: this is my objection
sentences.literal: Although you have reason, I insist: this is the my objection

words.note: The concession word that forces the congiuntivo. abbia, not hai, and the speaker is not in doubt: the mood is agreement with benché, nothing more.

words.cue: I insist, I stand by it
words.note: Holding your ground after a concession. It is not rude in Italian; it announces that the point survives what you have just admitted.
The noun for the thing you raise against a claim. It names the move, which is what lets you announce it before you make it.

sentences.trap: Benché tu hai ragione is wrong however certain you are. benché takes abbia whatever the sentence means; there is no meaning underneath to reason from.
sentences.sound: ben-KÉ, stress on the accented final e. in-SIS-to. o-bie-ZIO-ne.

variations.cue: Although you are right, I insist
variations.changed: the concession and the stand, with nothing named

variations.cue: Although you are right, I insist
variations.changed: the other concession word, same mood

variations.cue: This is my objection
variations.changed: the objection announced on its own

mistake.why: hai is the indicative. benché governs the congiuntivo unconditionally, so the verb has to be abbia even though the speaker is certain you are right.

sentences.usage: Conceding a point in a discussion and then holding your own anyway.
sentences.mnemonic: benché bends the verb, not the meaning.

sentences.display: Sebbene sia difficile, nessuno può obiettare
sentences.cue: Although it is difficult, nobody can object
sentences.literal: Although it be difficult, nobody can to object

words.note: The twin of benché and slightly more written. Same trigger, same congiuntivo, and the two are interchangeable in an argument.

words.cue: to object, to raise an objection
words.note: The verb beside the noun obiezione. obietta is he or she objects, obietti is you object; the infinitive is what follows può.

sentences.trap: nessuno può obiettare needs no second negative. L2-M10's nessuno already carries the negation when it stands in front of the verb.
sentences.sound: seb-BE-ne, double b held. o-biet-TA-re, stress on TA.

variations.cue: Although it is difficult, nobody objects
variations.changed: the finite verb in place of can plus infinitive

variations.display: Benché sia difficile, nessuno può obiettare
variations.cue: Although it is difficult, nobody can object

mistake.display: Sebbene è difficile, nessuno può obiettare
mistake.why: è is the indicative and sebbene never takes it. The difficulty is a plain fact and the verb still has to be sia.

sentences.usage: Granting that something is hard while claiming the case is still watertight.
sentences.mnemonic: sebbene and benché: two words, one mood.

sentences.display: Nonostante tutto, ammetto una cosa: sbagliando ho capito il motivo
sentences.cue: In spite of everything, I admit one thing: by getting it wrong I understood the reason
sentences.literal: Notwithstanding all, I admit one thing: mistaking I have understood the reason

words.note: Third of the concession words. Before a noun it needs nothing, as here; before a clause it takes the congiuntivo like benché and sebbene.
The move that buys you the right to insist afterwards. An argument that admits nothing is heard as a speech, not a case.

words.cue: by getting it wrong, through error
words.note: The gerund used adverbially: it says HOW something happened. Same ending as L2-M7's mangiando and parlando, but with no stare in front of it.

sentences.trap: sbagliando ho capito is not I was making mistakes. The bare gerund with no stare says by doing it, and the tense comes from the other verb.
sentences.sound: no-nos-TAN-te. am-MET-to, double m. sba-GLIAN-do, the gli as in L1's figlio.

variations.cue: In spite of everything, I admit one thing
variations.changed: the admission with nothing after it

variations.cue: By getting it wrong I understood the reason
Even getting it wrong, nothing changes
variations.changed: pur in front turns the gerund into a concession

mistake.display: Nonostante tutto, ammetto una cosa: sbagliavo e ho capito
mistake.why: The imperfetto tells you he used to be wrong. The gerund is what says by getting it wrong, in one word and with no second clause.

sentences.usage: Conceding the one point that costs you something, before you go on.
sentences.mnemonic: -ando with stare is happening; -ando alone is how.

sentences.display: D'altra parte il lavoro va avanti. Tuttavia, il tempo manca
sentences.cue: On the other hand the work is going ahead. However, there is no time
sentences.literal: Of other part the work goes ahead. However, the time lacks

words.note: The turn in an argument. The elision is part of the token: d'altra is one word and does not resolve through altra.
The answer to the turn. It OPENS its clause and never sits inside it, unlike English however.

sentences.trap: Il tempo, tuttavia, manca is the English shape. tuttavia goes first: Tuttavia, il tempo manca.
sentences.sound: DAL-tra PAR-te, one breath. tut-ta-VI-a, stress on the VI.

variations.display: D'altra parte il lavoro va avanti
variations.cue: On the other hand the work is going ahead
However, there is no time

mistake.display: Il lavoro va avanti, tuttavia il tempo manca
mistake.why: Not the word but the seam: tuttavia opens a NEW sentence. Hung off a comma it reads as ma with a suit on, and the contrast is lost.

sentences.usage: Turning your own argument round to look at the other side, then answering it.

sentences.display: Essendo già tardi, decido domani, purché tu sia d'accordo
sentences.cue: It being late already, I will decide tomorrow, provided you agree
sentences.literal: Being already late, I decide tomorrow, provided that you be in agreement

words.note: The gerund of essere, used adverbially for a reason: essendo tardi is since it is late. It carries no subject pronoun of its own.
A condition, not a concession, and it takes the same congiuntivo the concessions take. sia, never sei.

sentences.trap: Essendo tardi has no subject pronoun and needs none. The gerund carries the subject of the main verb, or an impersonal it, and adding one breaks it.
sentences.sound: es-SEN-do, double s. pur-KÉ, stress on the accented final e.

variations.cue: It being late already, I will decide tomorrow

variations.display: Purché tu sia d'accordo, decido domani
variations.cue: Provided you agree, I will decide tomorrow
variations.changed: the condition moved to the front

variations.cue: Having time, I will decide tomorrow

mistake.display: Essendo già tardi, decido domani, purché tu sei d'accordo
mistake.why: sei is the indicative. purché is in the same trigger class as benché and sebbene, so the verb after it is sia.

sentences.usage: Putting off a decision and naming the one condition you need.
sentences.mnemonic: purché buys a promise, and it pays in congiuntivo.

sentences.display: Sostengo la stessa cosa, a meno che non ci sia un problema
sentences.cue: I maintain the same thing, unless there is a problem
sentences.literal: I maintain the same thing, to less that not there be a problem

words.cue: I maintain, I hold, I argue
words.note: Stronger than penso and weaker than insisto: it says this is my position and I have reasons. The claim word of an argument.
Three words, one key, and the non that follows is not a negative. a meno che non piova is unless it rains.

sentences.trap: The non after a meno che negates nothing. Reading it as a real negative flips the sentence: this says unless there IS a problem.
sentences.sound: sos-TEN-go. a ME-no ke, three light words run together.

variations.cue: I maintain the same thing

variations.display: A meno che non ci sia un'altra obiezione, ho finito
variations.cue: Unless there is another objection, I have finished
variations.changed: the exception carrying the whole sentence

mistake.display: Sostengo la stessa cosa, a meno che ci sia un problema
mistake.why: The non is missing. It is not optional in written or careful Italian: a meno che comes with it, exactly as L4-M6's finché non does.

sentences.usage: Stating your position and naming the single thing that would change it.
sentences.mnemonic: a meno che non: the non is part of the word, not part of the meaning.

sentences.display: Pur essendo d'accordo, non cambia niente. Pur avendo ragione, non insisto
sentences.cue: Even though I agree, nothing changes. Even though I am right, I do not insist
sentences.literal: Even being in agreement, not changes nothing. Even having reason, not I insist

words.note: The compressed concession: two words where benché needs a whole clause with a congiuntivo in it. Learned whole, because it is used whole.
pur in front of any gerund makes it concessive. Without pur, avendo ragione is because he is right; with it, although he is right.
The gerund of avere. It gives a reason on its own and a concession behind pur, and it never takes a subject pronoun.

sentences.trap: Pur essendo d'accordo has no che and no congiuntivo. It is the SHORT road round benché, not a version of it.
sentences.sound: pur es-SEN-do. pur a-VEN-do, the r of pur runs straight into the vowel.

variations.display: Pur essendo d'accordo, non cambia niente
variations.cue: Even though I agree, nothing changes
Even though I am right, I do not insist
Even getting it wrong, nothing changes
variations.changed: a third verb in the same frame

mistake.display: Pur essendo che sono d'accordo, non cambia niente
mistake.why: pur essendo IS the clause. Adding che and a finite verb builds the thing the phrase exists to avoid.

sentences.usage: Giving ground in the shortest form Italian has, usually in the middle of a longer point.
sentences.mnemonic: pur + -ando or -endo = although, in two words.

sentences.display: In conclusione, lo spiego affinché sia tutto giusto, prima che sia tardi
sentences.cue: In conclusion, I am explaining it so that everything is right, before it is too late
sentences.literal: In conclusion, it I explain so that be all right, before that be late

words.note: The last rung of the scaffold. It announces that what follows is the close, so nobody has to guess whether you are still adding points.
Purpose, and another congiuntivo trigger. Two subjects: I explain so that IT is right; with one subject Italian uses per plus the infinitive.
The different-subject twin of L4-M6's prima di. prima di partire when it is you leaving; prima che sia tardi when it is something else.

sentences.trap: prima di takes an infinitive and prima che takes a congiuntivo. The choice is made by whether the two verbs share a subject, not by the meaning.
sentences.sound: in con-clu-SIO-ne. af-fin-KÉ, stress on the accented final e. PRI-ma ke.

variations.display: In conclusione, lo spiego affinché sia tutto giusto
variations.cue: In conclusion, I am explaining it so that everything is right

variations.display: Lo spiego prima che sia tardi
variations.cue: I am explaining it before it is too late

mistake.display: In conclusione, lo spiego affinché è tutto giusto
mistake.why: affinché is a trigger like benché and purché. Purpose is never stated with the indicative, however certain the outcome.

sentences.usage: Closing a case: what you want out of it, and by when.
sentences.mnemonic: prima DI you, prima CHE it.

comprehensionPool.cue: First of all, there is no time

comprehensionPool.display: Il fatto è che nessuno capisce
comprehensionPool.cue: The fact is that nobody understands

comprehensionPool.cue: Although it is difficult, I insist

comprehensionPool.display: D'altra parte, ad esempio, nessuno dorme

comprehensionPool.display: Tuttavia, in conclusione, il problema resta
